learning: If this race reproduces about 111.8, the platform and controller are confirmed. The next lever is inertia at the midpoint (mass 0.75, body_length 0.16), which the Builder has proposed. If slalom line loss is 0.2 or higher, the controller is not the cause, and inertia is.
notes: Iteration-5 platform with the proven iteration-1/5 controller, so the race tests the Builder's revert on a known baseline. The controller is unchanged, to avoid confounding the revert with new gains.
rationale: The Builder's geometry for this iteration is the iteration-5 platform: wheel_track 0.12, mass 0.8, body_length 0.18, five sensors at x -0.06 to +0.06 in 0.03 m steps, y 0.03, 16 mm footprints. Iteration 5 raced this platform with the controller below and scored 111.80. Slalom line loss was 0.10, oval progress 0.55, and s-bend progress 0.14. The only platform change that clearly raised score, lower inertia (iteration 4, 124.20), pushed slalom line loss to 0.85, so inertia stays here. Narrowing the track to 0.10 (iterations 6 to 8) cut oval progress to about 0.28 to 0.30 and scored 72.9 to 79.6 across kp 2.5 to 3.0, so the 0.10 track is rejected. Every controller change tried on this platform was confounded with a geometry change except kp 4 and kd 0.6 (iteration 2) and the kp and base_speed softening (iteration 3). Both made line loss worse. I therefore keep the one controller that has raced on this exact geometry with the best result (kp 3.0, kd 0.3, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.2, last_direction). Changing gains now would add risk without evidence. max_error sits at 0.061 to 0.066 m on every geometry, so it is most likely the run-ending threshold, not a tuning target. Expected result: a score near 111.8 (range about 110 to 120), with slalom line loss near 0.1.
